response.answer: David Hockney's exhibition "David Hockney: Portraits in Print" is on display at the National Gallery of Australia from September 5, 2026, to May 9, 2027. The exhibition features traditional mediums like etching, lithography, and photography alongside experimental tools such as mylar sheets and fax machines, showcasing Hockney's exploration of different art mediums even in his 80s. results.title: A Buyer’s Guide To David Hockney
results.content:
Exhibition posters and unsigned works form a separate category within the Hockney print market. While they do not carry the same long-term resale potential as numbered editions, original period posters can provide an accessible entry point for new collectors.

Buyers should distinguish clearly between original exhibition posters and later reproductions, and verify condition carefully before purchase.

“David Hockney is continually reaching out for that flame and he is endlessly curious.” [...] Other high-performing works include Afternoon Swimming (edition of 55), which has traded around £360,000, and digital landscapes such as A Bigger Green Valley, which has surpassed £300,000. Within Moving Focus, standout compositions such as Caribbean Tea Time have also exceeded £300,000. [...] These works feature vivid colour, layered composition, and strong visual immediacy. Not all digital prints were produced in identical edition sizes, and smaller editions tend to command stronger buyer interest. Overlooked in that canon is a stranger, more private painting: _Beverly Hills Housewife_, a 12-foot portrait that Hockney painted between 1966 and ’67. A new book by critic and curator James Cahill, out in the U.K. now and in the U.S. on November 3, argues the painting captures the artist’s new, “crystalline realist” style, and ultimately reveals two people—the artist and the subject—caught in a moment of transformation.

results.title: The year in review: Influential people who have died in 2026
results.content:
David Hockney, 88. He was a treasured British artist whose paintings of shimmering pools and colorful iPad drawings became icons of contemporary art. June 11.

Ronnie Schell, 94. He played the best friend to the title character on the 1960s sitcom “Gomer Pyle, U.S.M.C.” and his gradual ascendancy in show business earned him the title of “America’s Slowest Rising Comedian.” June 12.
